# Landau fan — VTI variant

**Base**: `measurements/landau-fan.md`. This file carries only the deltas
(STYLE rule 13); read the base first. Runs executed under this variant tag
`s.add_comment('landau-fan-vti')`.

The base's Recipe steps are toploader-flavored in their call surface (driver
names, an explicit field-settle sleep, a Discord ping). On the VTI those
names and the settle discipline differ; the *method* — coarse-first design,
both-axis Nyquist, Středa read — is unchanged.

**Overridden steps and the rig facts that force them:**

- **Steps 0/5, field parameter** — the field parameter is
  **`magnet.field`** (the instrument instance is named `magnet`, not `mag`);
  the station builder is `sweep.AsyncStation(mc)`, same as the base. The
  slow-axis call is
  `s.multimegasweep([magnet.field], [B_vec], [k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [Vtgs, Vbgs], slow_delay=…, fast_delay=…)`.
- **Step 2, fast axis** — the gate-voltage helper is
  `sharpelab_nb.gates.calc_gate_voltages(n, D, c_tg, c_bg, n_offset, D_offset)`
  (the `(c_tg, c_bg, offsets)` form written back by
  `cnp-and-dline-calibration`), not `calculate_gate_voltages(ns, Ds, dtg=, dbg=)`.
- **Step 4, field positioning** — `magnet.field(target)` **blocks until the
  field is reached** (FastBi1K5 blocking ramp; see the rig card's magnet
  Set-semantics). So there is **no `time.sleep(600)` pre-settle** — the set
  call *is* the settle. Position by `magnet.field(B_start)` and proceed.
- **Step 8, notify** — `hera-notify` on the operator's key (rig notify
  channel), not `alerts.discord`.
- **Step 6, fp list** — follow the rig card's instrument-polling rules when
  building the `fp` set; the card names which instruments are unsafe to poll
  per-point on this rig. *(The base says "fp temperature(s)"; the card
  governs — do not restate the hazard here.)*

**Cost-model regime (base Why).** The base's "finer B steps cost only row
turnaround, and coarsening B buys aliasing, not time" corollary holds only
when the grid is cheap relative to the traverse. On the VTI the magnet is
blocking-ramp-limited (so the traverse term is fixed by the B-span) **but
per-point time is ~1.2–1.4 s/pt** (rig card Timing; ~1.44 s/pt at a 4τ
settle), which makes a multi-tesla fan **measurement-dominated** — the bare
traverse (~1 h at 8 T) is small against the grid. So the base's
*measurement-dominated* branch applies: buy the high-n Nyquist floor (base
step 1, the n_max re-check) by **trimming n-points or flooring the high-n
claim**, never by adding B rows blindly. "Fine B is nearly free" is a
toploader-era (non-blocking-magnet, traverse-dominated) statement; do not
carry it to this rig.

## Examples

- A VTI trilayer fan *(our-measurement, 2026-06-14)*: `file_id 20`, D = 0,
  0 → 8 T paired n-line, `magnet.field` slow axis, ~1.44 s/pt at a 4τ dwell —
  the measurement-dominated regime above (8 T bare traverse ≈ 1 h ≪ grid
  time). The firming fan `file_id 21` rode the magnet home (8 → 0 T) as a
  measured ramp-down, picking up high-n rows on the way — the base's
  "plan the direction so the fan ends where the next measurement needs it".

## Next

Base `## Next` applies unchanged.

## Obsolescence

Delete this file when the base recipe goes fully instrument-class-conditional
(driver names — `magnet.field`, the notify channel — move
to the rig card, leaving the base name-free): the cost-regime note then folds
into the base's rig-property cost discussion, and the settle/fast-axis deltas
become base conditionals the rig card resolves. Moving fans onto a continuous
on-the-fly ramp (the driver's `start_field_ramp` + sampled readback, outside
the blocking `sweep` set) would also retire the step-4 delta.
# SdH spot check

## What
A fixed-(n, D) magnetic-field sweep over a **low-field window**, designed to resolve
Shubnikov–de Haas / quantum-oscillation **frequency content** at one density — the
onset field and the tone frequencies — by FFT in 1/B. Mechanically this is a
`field-sweep-1d` (see it for the Station / sweep / fp / plot call surface); what
makes it a *spot check* is the design discipline below — the field range, 1/B spacing
Δ(1/B), and settling are chosen to resolve the tones cleanly, and the read is the 1/B
FFT.
It is the cheap 1D precursor to a `landau-fan`: one density, but **full per-point
quality**.

## When
- **Before committing a `landau-fan`.** A spot check pins the **onset** (sets the
  fan's B-range), the **observed tone frequencies** (confirm/correct the fan's
  Δ(1/B)), and the **settling/sensitivity** the fan inherits. A fan is the dense
  version; a couple of clean spot checks de-risk it — and can answer the question
  outright (`investigations/trilayer-stacking-fs-count.md` Step 3).
- Whenever a `field-sweep-1d` or `gatemap` showed QO-like wiggles and you want the
  frequency content at a point, not the whole (n, B) plane.

## Why
A spot check is cheap because it is **one density (1D), not because it is
low-quality**. Its whole value is being acquired *well* — at the settling floor and
Nyquist on the fastest tone — so a clean spot check can be decisive on its own and a
noisier fan cannot overturn it (`landau-fan`). Two knobs carry the quality:

- **Sampling.** The fastest tone sets the finest 1/B period. The reference frequency
  **F_L = (h/g·e)·n** (g = 4) — what a single four-fold pocket carrying all the
  density would give — is an upper bound on the fastest tone; Nyquist it. Undersampling
  the fast tone folds its aliases into the low-frequency band, where they masquerade
  as a small/slow tone (Verify).
- **Settling.** A swept-point dwell has a floor near the lock-in time constant
  (dwell ≥ k·τ; k ≈ 5 at 6 dB/oct, 7–10 at 24 dB/oct). Under-settling **attenuates
  the oscillation amplitude itself** (the filter cannot track the QO) — benign on a
  smooth slope, but it *buries a small tone* (Verify). The floor is non-negotiable
  when the target is a weak tone.

## Recipe
1. **Density + range.** Pick the density — high |n| gives the most periods and the
   clearest tones. Sweep a field window **[B_lo, B_hi]**; the sampling grid follows
   the magnet class:
   - **Field moves cheap** (non-blocking magnet): sample **uniformly in 1/B**
     (`field_invB`) — constant points-per-period, FFT the raw points (no resample).
     `B_lo` is a small positive floor (~0.1–0.3 T) below the expected **onset** (the
     lowest B where oscillations emerge once the MR background is subtracted) —
     uniform-1/B is densest in B at low field, so it captures the onset for free.
   - **Blocking rate-limited magnet** (traverse dominates wall-clock): sample
     **uniformly in B** with **ΔB = Δ(1/B)·B_lo²** (Nyquist held at the low-B edge;
     `sdh_fft` resamples internally). Same wall-clock — the points ride the traverse —
     with ≳30× the per-period averaging at high B and no blind ramps between sparse
     high-B points. ΔB scales as B_lo², so put `B_lo` just below the expected onset,
     not at a deep floor.
2. **Δ(1/B) from F_L.** Compute F_L = (h/4e)·n and Nyquist-resolve it: Δ(1/B) ≤ 1/(2·F_L)
   (prefer 1/3). Set N from the window: N = (1/B_lo − 1/B_hi)/Δ(1/B) + 1 uniform-1/B,
   N = (B_hi − B_lo)/ΔB + 1 uniform-B. This Δ(1/B) (and N) is what a committed fan
   inherits.
3. **δF from the record.** The tone resolution is set by the usable 1/B record above
   onset: **δF = 1/(1/B_onset − 1/B_max)** — tones closer than ~δF merge; trust a
   split only past ~2·δF. On high-T_e rigs the onset, not the field cap, sets δF:
   once 1/B_max ≪ 1/B_onset, raising B_max buys little — the lever is the
   density/side with the lower onset. Compute δF against the tones the claim must
   separate before sweeping.
4. **Lock-in.** Set sensitivity so full scale ≈ I_bias × R_target — a signal at a
   few % of range is coarse-ADC digitized (the grainy-FFT failure). Set the dwell at
   the settling floor (Why); read τ and the filter slope, do not guess them.
5. **The sweep.** Run it as a `field-sweep-1d` (its Recipe is the call surface):
   build the Station, ramp the gates to (n, D), `s.sweep(mag.field, B_vec,
   delay=dwell)` with the step-1 grid, fp the temperature(s) and every lock-in X/P,
   plot the live MR and gate-current leakage.
6. **FFT read.** Re-form Rxx from the TSV (rendered PNGs alias).
   - **Onset** — `hera.analysis.sdh_onset(R, B)` returns an `SdhOnset`: `onset_b` is
     the low-B edge of usable oscillation content (minimum over the tracked tones —
     a light tone that outlives the dominant one carries it), `clip_high_b` the high
     edge. `tones` holds each tone's own track: `freq`, per-tone `onset_b`,
     `snr`/`amp` curves over `b_centers`, `delta_f(b_max)` (that tone's usable-record
     resolution), and flags — `censored` (still above threshold at the record's low
     edge: `onset_b` is the record edge, not a measured die-off), `revived`,
     `marginal`, `near_residual`, and the bidirectional harmonic pair
     `harmonic_of` (this tone sits at k× a lower tone) / `harmonics` (freqs of
     tones sitting at k× of this one — a comb member is flagged from both ends
     regardless of which is stronger). Print `on.summary()` in the read
     cell. Pass `r_full_scale = sensitivity / I_bias` so a soft-clipped channel
     truncates the analysis window (with a warning) instead of feeding a flat-topped
     record to the FFT. Failure raises `SdhOnsetError` naming what was untrackable —
     that is a read result (no usable oscillations), not a prompt to eyeball.
   - **FFT** — `hera.analysis.sdh_fft(R_grid, B, *, b_range=(cutoff, B_max), bg_degree=5)`
     takes `R_grid` as `(n_B, n_fast)` — pass a single trace as `R[:, None]` — removes
     the MR background with a degree-`bg_degree` polynomial **in B** (the background is
     smooth in B, not 1/B), then FFTs in 1/B per column, and returns
     `(freqs, spec[n_fast, n_freq])` with `freqs` in Tesla. It needs a field range wide enough that
     the polynomial captures the background without absorbing the oscillations.
     `cutoff ≥ onset_b`, and often **above** it (Verify). Read the **tone frequencies**
     against F_L.

## Verify
- **Settling — under-settling buries a small tone.** A dwell below the floor
  attenuates the oscillation amplitude (the filter can't track it). On a smooth slope
  that's a benign uniform lag; when the target is a small/weak tone it *erases* the
  feature. Non-negotiable for a weak-tone hunt; bend it only for a slope read on a
  strong signal.
- **Sampling — an undersampled fast tone aliases down.** If Δ(1/B) under-samples the
  fastest tone (≈ F_L), its aliases fold into the low-frequency band and masquerade
  as a small/slow tone. Nyquist the *fast* tone even when the target is the slow one
  (worked case: Examples).
- **Grid-change reproduction separates tones from aliases.** A real tone survives a
  change of sampling scheme (uniform-B vs uniform-1/B); an alias moves with the grid.
- **FFT stability sweep.** Vary `bg_degree` and the window; a real peak **sharpens**
  as the 1/B record lengthens, an alias/artifact **wanders**.
- **Onset is read from the background-subtracted data, not the FFT.** It is the
  low-field point where oscillations emerge in ΔRxx(B) (the MR background removed), not
  a quantity the FFT returns. It is a **lower bound** on the FFT low-field cutoff:
  residual background near the low-B end inflates the slowest tones, so raise the cutoff
  above the onset until the slow-tone amplitudes stop shrinking. Report the onset — it
  sets a fan's B-range and tracks quantum mobility (a rise on a later cooldown is a
  device-quality regression).

## Examples
- *(our-measurement)* — a fine-step spot check resolved two tones (a main tone + a
  low-frequency partner), where a same-session fan run at a coarser B-step and
  under-settled did not. An earlier 4× coarser step had under-sampled the main tone,
  folding its aliases into the small-tone band. The worked case for "acquire the
  spot check well, *then* commit the fan."

## Next
- **Clean QO, tones resolved** → run a `landau-fan`, inheriting this spot check's

# Tetralayer FS-count forward model — ABAB vs ABCA (vs ABCB)

Backs the `recipes/investigations/tetralayer-stacking-fs-count.md` investigation.
This model computes the **B = 0 Fermi-surface count**, the **Onsager
frequencies F(n)** (and vs interlayer potential u_D for ABCA), and the
**cyclotron masses m\*(n)** the FS-count read overlays on data — ABAB a pair
partitioning F_L (≈ 0.72 / 0.28 with φ²-split masses in the decomposition
limit; the key table below carries the real F(n)) vs ABCA's single
post-cascade pocket at F_L, with ABCB a qualitative cubic + Dirac pair.
**Both carrier signs**: the sign of the input density selects electron
(n > 0) or hole (n < 0) doping.

The survey that grounds it (band structure, the four ingested papers, the
feasibility framing) is `docs/tetralayer-stacking-extraction-survey.md`; read
it for the physics. This README covers what the tools are and how to run them.

## Files

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| `synth_fan.py` | Synthetic Rxx(n, B) fan generator on the model's F(n)/m\*(n): LK thermal + Dingle dressing, 2nd harmonics, background, noise; optional lever-arm scale error, breakdown sum-tone, mixed-domain superposition. Ground truth per column in `truth.json`. |
| `synth_eval.py` | Mechanical recipe evaluator over the synthetic fans (pipeline FFT → Luttinger-aware harmonic screen → global scale pin → template match → B-window split → adjacent-N). Six-case suite + `RESULTS.md` in `$HERA_DATA/tetralayer-synth-validation/`. |
| `JULIA_CROSSCHECK.md` | Independent-implementation eigenvalue comparison (machine precision; see Validation). |
| `fs_count_b0.py` | B = 0 FS count + Onsager F(n) + m\*(n), both carrier signs. **ABAB** from the 2N-band SWMcC Hamiltonian (Koshino–McCann PRB 83, 165443 Eq. 1, N = 4), graphite parameters, via a rotationally-symmetric signed-density radial solve (electron pockets +k²/π, hole pockets −k²/π; the two bilayer-like blocks emerge automatically). **ABCA** from the 8-band continuum model of arXiv 2606.05356 S15 (Eqs. 8–14), parameter Set 1, on a 2D k-grid (trigonal warping → the low-density three-pocket → annulus → single Lifshitz cascade); interlayer potential u_D via the onsite U_l structure. **ABCB** qualitative, via the generic linkage builder. A generic `build_h(kx, ky, seq, p, ud)` dispatches any stacking string ('ABAB','ABCA','ABA','ABC',…) to a Bernal / rhombohedral / mixed block builder by link sense, so trilayer sequences run for backtests. Counts distinct extremal-orbit frequencies F = (ℏ/2πe)·A_k, positive/area-based for electron- and hole-like orbits alike. Pure numpy/scipy; `selftest()`/`__main__` runs every validation gate and prints the key tables. |

## API (call shapes)

- `abab_fs(n, ud=0.0) -> (E_F, [(F, kF), ...])` — every ABAB Onsager orbit at
  E_F, sorted by F.
- `abab_mstar(n, ud=0.0) -> [(F, m*/m_e), ...]` — per-orbit cyclotron masses,
  m\* = ℏ²k_F/|dE/dk|, same orbits/order as `abab_fs`.
- `abca_fs(n, ud=0.0) -> (E_F, topo, n_components, n_freq, F_total)` — topology
  from connected components of the Fermi sea (single / annulus / k-pocket).
- `abca_mstar(n, ud=0.0) -> (F_total, m*/m_e)` — from dn/dE_F on the same solve;
  pocket-summed in the cascade region.
- `abcb_fs(n, ud=0.0) -> (E_F, [(F, ncomp), ...])` — **qualitative**, electron
  side only: the two low-energy conduction tones (cubic J = 3 + Dirac J = 1).
- Generic underneath: `bernal_fs`/`bernal_mstar`/`rhombo_fs`/`rhombo_mstar`
  take a sequence + `Params`; `build_h(kx, ky, seq, p, ud)` returns the
  Hamiltonian; `ABAB`, `ABCA`, `ABA_TRI` are the parameter sets.

Masses are positive for electron- and hole-like orbits alike; the carrier sign
comes from the input n.

## Domain — loud, never clamped

The solvers raise `ValueError` (naming the covered range) for any density
outside the solved table; E_F rows whose Fermi contour would cross the k-grid
edge are excluded from the table on both sides. Solved coverage at u_D = 0:
ABAB ≈ −17.7…+17.1 ×10¹² cm⁻², ABCA ≈ ±11.5 ×10¹² cm⁻² — comfortably beyond
the ±8×10¹² cm⁻² design target.

## Parameters and validity

**Semi-quantitative — trust topology, shape, and partition, not absolute
frequencies.** The discriminating outputs are the FS count, the ABAB partition
and its φ²-split masses, and the model-independent Luttinger sum
Σ±f = (h/4e)|n|. Absolute frequencies inherit the hopping-parameter error bars.

- **ABAB**: Koshino–McCann graphite SWMcC set {γ₀ = 3.0, γ₁ = 0.4, γ₂ = −0.02,
  γ₄ = 0.04, γ₅ = 0.04, Δ′ = 0.05 eV}, all remote couplings ON. **γ₃ = 0**:
  the BL-contour trigonal warping is neglected so the solve stays radial (same
  precedent and caveat as the trilayer ABA treatment — γ₃ touches only the
  low-|n| BL fine structure). The 0.724 / 0.276 partition and φ² ≈ 2.618 mass
  ratio are the **low-n parabolic (decomposition) asymptote**; two effects
  distort them away from it — non-parabolicity (the bilayer bands bend toward
  linear) pulls the ratio *down* with rising |n|, while the γ₂-scale
  band-bottom offset dominates at low |n| and washes out with rising |n|. In
  the full model the electron-side partition passes through ≈ 0.73 near
  |n| ≈ 6×10¹²; the hole side runs lower (≈ 0.64) from the Δ′/γ₄ e–h asymmetry
  and the near-CNP semimetal overlap (§ below). Even-N has no mirror plane, so
  the two bilayer blocks are mixed by γ₂/γ₅ at the ~20 meV scale and inter-block
  magnetic breakdown is symmetry-allowed — the two-FS picture is exact only
  above that scale.
- **ABCA**: arXiv 2606.05356 S15 Set 1 {γ₀ = 3.1, γ₁ = 0.38, γ₂ = −0.015,
  γ₃ = 0.29, γ₄ = 0.141, δ = 0.0105, Δ₂ = 0.002 eV}, **γ₃ ON** (trigonal
  warping is the physics of the low-density cascade, not fine structure).
  u_D enters as a linear interlayer potential V_l = l·u_D (no Hartree screening).
  At operating density (|n| ≳ 2×10¹²) the pocket is single and F(n) is
  Luttinger-solid ((h/4e)|n| by area conservation), insensitive to the
  parameter error bars.
- **ABCB**: qualitative only, via the mixed-linkage builder run on the ABCA
  hopping magnitudes. Reproduces the J = 3 cubic main band + J = 1 Dirac-like
  partner rising from the ~δ (≈ 10 meV) gap; the two tones Luttinger-sum to
  F_L. **Absolute frequencies and the partition are not calibrated** — trust
  the two-tone topology and order of magnitude only. Not gated.
- ABAB is semimetallic near the CNP: for small |n| tiny electron and hole
  pockets coexist (the two blocks' band bottoms are offset at the γ₂ scale),
  the orbit list reports all of them, and only the **signed** sum of
  frequencies equals (h/4e)|n| there.

## Validation

All six gates pass (`selftest()`); residuals quoted are the actual run.

- **Gate 1 — ABAB decomposition limit**: with γ₂ = γ₅ = Δ′ = γ₄ = γ₃ = 0 the
  k = 0 spectrum is {±0.618γ₁, ±1.618γ₁, 0×4} (λ = 2cos2π/5, 2cos π/5) to
  1.7×10⁻¹² eV; the high-density Onsager partition → 0.7236 / 0.2764 and mass
  ratio → 2.618 in the low-n parabolic limit (0.722 / 2.574 at |n| = 0.25×10¹²,
  monotonically degrading with non-parabolicity: 0.692 / 2.01 at 6×10¹²).
- **Gate 2 — Luttinger sum** Σ±f = (h/4e)|n| reproduces on **both carrier
  signs** for ABAB (signed) and ABCA (single pocket) at every density tested
  (worst residual 0.015 T, grid discretization).
- **Gate 3a — ABCA higher-order vHS**: the analytic E₂ (S15 Eq. 17) crosses
  zero at the critical u_D solving Eq. 18, u_D = 42.82 meV; the numerical
  lowest-conduction-band k → 0 curvature flips sign at 43 meV, tracking E₂ to
  ≤ 0.3% across u_D ∈ [30, 55] meV.
- **Gate 3b — ABCA Lifshitz cascade**: at u_D = 43 meV the Fermi sea passes
  **three-pocket → annulus → single** as n grows (topology sequence matches
  Fig S29-c). Boundaries land at n ≈ 1.5 / 2.6 ×10¹² — ~2–4× above the S29-c
  digitization; **qualitative agreement only** (topology + order of magnitude),
  as scoped by the survey.
- **Gate 4 — trilayer backtest**: the generic builder run as 'ABA' with the
  frozen `models/trilayer_fs_count` parameters reproduces that model's
  `aba_fs` F(n) at n = ±{1,2,3,6}×10¹² to **≤ 0.17%** (e.g. +6×10¹²:

  The generic 'ABC' single-pocket F(n) matches (h/4e)|n| to 0.01% (Luttinger —
  the frozen ABC is a MacDonald two-band projection, so only its
  Luttinger-pinned F is comparable).
- **Gate 5 — m\* identities**: ABAB per-orbit masses satisfy the thermodynamic
  DOS identity dn/dE = (2/πℏ²)·Σ±m\* against the density table (worst 0.2%);
  ABCA m\* matches an independent finite-difference of E_F(n) (worst 1.7%).

  `$HERA_DATA/tetralayer-synth-validation/RESULTS.md`): six dressed synthetic
  fans (clean ABAB hole/electron incl. the low-n trap, clean ABCA, breakdown

- **Agent-in-harness replay (rung 3b + adjacent-N amendment)** — three
  classification-frontier fixtures
  (`hera/test-cases/{2026-05-14-QC0512,2026-05-21-QC0531,2026-02-17-RPL19}-stacking-fan`)

- **Julia cross-check** (`JULIA_CROSSCHECK.md`): `h_rhombo` agrees with the
  independent `RhombohedralGrapheneLandau.jl` implementation at the

def open_run(path: str | Path) -> Run:
    """Open a sweep run directory — completed or in flight.

    `path` is the run dir (e.g. `<notebook>/data/119`). Must contain
    `metadata.json` and either `data.tsv.gz` or `data.tsv`. Column names
    come from metadata — TSVs are headerless, and sweep writes `columns`
    to `metadata.json` at sweep start, so names resolve mid-run too. An
    in-flight run's TSV may end mid-row; only newline-terminated rows are
    trusted (sweep writes row-at-a-time, so interior lines are whole).
    """
    path = Path(path).expanduser().resolve()
    if not path.is_dir():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"not a directory: {path}")

    meta_path = path / "metadata.json"
    if not meta_path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"missing metadata.json in {path}")
    meta = json.loads(meta_path.read_text())

    cols = list(meta.get("columns") or [])
    if not cols:
        raise ValueError(f"metadata.json has no 'columns' entry in {path}")

    tsv_gz = path / "data.tsv.gz"
    tsv = path / "data.tsv"
    if tsv_gz.exists():
        raw = gzip.decompress(tsv_gz.read_bytes())
    elif tsv.exists():
        raw = tsv.read_bytes()
    else:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no data.tsv(.gz) in {path}")

    text = raw.decode("utf-8").replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n")
    if text and not text.endswith("\n"):
        text = text[: text.rfind("\n") + 1]  # drop the row still being written

    if text.strip():
        data = np.loadtxt(io.StringIO(text), delimiter="\t", ndmin=2)
    else:
        data = np.empty((0, len(cols)), dtype=float)

    if data.shape[1] != len(cols):
        raise ValueError(
            f"column count mismatch in {path}: data has {data.shape[1]} "
            f"cols, metadata declares {len(cols)}"
        )

    return Run(path=path, meta=meta, cols=cols, data=data)

                        [--markdown-file PATH] [--code-file PATH]

                        notebook

Appends markdown and/or code cells at the end of a JupyterLab-open notebook
via the YDoc/RTC channel. Inserted cells are tagged metadata.hera (a dict
carrying the version tag and an appended_at UTC timestamp) so they can be
filtered and timed later. Re-running with the same args double-inserts.

positional arguments:
  notebook              Path to .ipynb (absolute or relative to cwd).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --markdown TEXT       Append a markdown cell with this source. Pass '-' to
                        read the cell from stdin; multiple '-' flags consume
                        successive chunks separated by a line of '---|'.
                        Repeatable; order preserved across all
                        --markdown/--code variants.
  --code TEXT           Append an un-executed code cell with this source. Pass
                        '-' to read the cell from stdin (see --markdown for
                        chunk semantics). Repeatable; order preserved across
                        all --markdown/--code variants.
  --markdown-file PATH  Append a markdown cell whose source is read from PATH
                        (UTF-8). Repeatable; order-preserved.
  --code-file PATH      Append an un-executed code cell whose source is read
                        from PATH (UTF-8). Repeatable; order-preserved.
  --summary TEXT        One-line dense spec of the proposed measurement.
                        Rendered into the FIRST appended markdown cell, right
                        after its leading heading (or prepended if the cell
                        has none) as a timestamped blockquote: '> **14:32** ·
                        <summary>' — the clock is server-local time at append;
                        _/* in the text are escaped for rendering. Also
                        stamped verbatim to metadata.hera.summary on that
                        cell. Requires at least one markdown cell among the
                        appended cells (--markdown/--markdown-file); must not
                        contain a backtick. At most once.
  --eta DURATION        Expected runtime for the proposed measurement — '40m',
                        '2h', or '1h30m' (optional <N>h then optional <N>m, h
                        before m; at least one required, total > 0; fractional
                        values rejected). A bare number like '40' is REJECTED
                        — add the m/h suffix. Rendered into the FIRST appended
                        markdown cell's blockquote line (with --summary or
                        alone) as '**ETA ~15:12** (≈40 min)' in server-local
                        time, computed from the same append instant; crossing
                        local midnight adds ' (+1d)' right after the clock.
                        Also stamped as an ISO-8601 UTC instant to
                        metadata.hera.eta_at on that cell, and echoed to
                        stdout as 'eta: ~15:12 (≈40 min)'. Requires at least
                        one markdown cell among the appended cells. At most
                        once.
  --execute             After appending, run the last appended code cell
                        YOURSELF by the id this append just created (never
                        nb['cells'][-1] off the stale on-disk file). Policy-
                        gated like execute-cell (append_exec or edit_exec),
                        checked before any cell lands. Exit code reflects the
                        cell's status. Mutually exclusive with --wait.
  --wait                After appending, block until the OPERATOR runs the
                        last appended code cell (its execution_count flips
                        non-null) — append + wait in one call, no cell id to
                        capture by hand. Does NOT execute anything, so it is
                        permitted on an append_only (E0) measure notebook.
                        Pair with --follow to background a no-deadline wait.
                        Mutually exclusive with --execute.
  --follow              With --wait: lift the deadline entirely (no timeout)
                        for a backgrounded wait. Use with run_in_background so
                        a foreground call cannot hang past the harness's ~600s
                        shell cap.
  --server-url SERVER_URL
                        Override server URL (default: auto-discover).
  --token TOKEN         Override server token (default: auto-discover).
  --settle SETTLE       Seconds to wait after appending before disconnecting.
                        Default 0.5.
  --timeout TIMEOUT     Foreground deadline (seconds) for --execute (cell run)

                        prefer --follow to background a no-deadline wait; a
                        timeout is loud and distinct (status: TIMEOUT, stderr
                        line, exit 2).
  --poll POLL           With --wait: polling interval in seconds. Default 1.0.

# CNP-line and D-line calibration

*Base recipe, rig-agnostic. Mostly analysis: it consumes the cooldown's
first 0 T gate map and produces the validated (n, D) conversion and the
constant-D line designer that every coordinate-claiming recipe downstream
(`landau-fan`, `nD-map`, feature positions) inherits. The house
conversion is the capacitance form — `sharpelab_nb.gates`:
`stack_capacitance` / `calc_nD` / `calc_gate_voltages` — with the
device's numbers in the device card. (The legacy thickness-parametrized
`calculate_n_D` is the single-dielectric special case of the same
helpers; older notebooks also carry inline equivalents — use those only
to replot their own runs.)*

## What
From a 0 T gate map: locate the charge-neutrality ridge per channel, fit
the CNP line in (V_tg, V_bg), refine the gate-capacitance **ratio** from
its slope (a fitted CNP slope dV_tg/dV_bg *is* −c_bg/c_tg), set the
density offset from its intercept, and emit constant-D gate-voltage
lines clipped to the validators. Output is a calibration contract
written to the device card: per-channel fits, the chosen (c_tg, c_bg)
with provenance split — **ratio: data-calibrated; absolute scale:
geometry prior until a quantum-Hall lever-arm check upgrades it** — the
offsets, a residual quality number, and the D-line designer parameters.

## When
After `gate-range-finding` (validators committed) and a first `gatemap`
that shows the CNP crossing the swept window. Re-run when:
- the operating point of a screening gate changes (the CNP intercept
  shifts with it; the slope usually survives — verify, don't assume);
- `reentry-baseline` shows feature-position drift across a handover;
- quantum-Hall data lands and enables the lever-arm upgrade (step 5).

No new sweeps are required if the gatemap is adequate; if the CNP exits
the window or is clipped (step 1 guard), this recipe specifies the map
extension and hands back to `gatemap`.

## Why
Every (n, D)-coordinate claim downstream inherits this calibration:
wrong capacitances tilt a fan's co-swept fast axis (the "fixed D" line
silently varies in D), shift every filling-factor assignment, and move
feature positions between sessions. The CNP slope is the cheapest
precise calibration in the corpus — one polyfit on a map you already
have — and it measures exactly the quantity the conversion needs
(c_bg/c_tg). What it does **not** measure is the absolute scale: slope
and intercept are invariant under c → λc, so n and D magnitudes carry
the geometry prior's uncertainty until ray slopes (dn/dB = ν·e/h) or
SdH frequencies pin the scale. Keep the two tiers separate in every
write-back; an absolute-n claim quoted at ratio-grade precision is a
provenance error (STYLE rule 5).

## Recipe

**Step 0 — inputs.** Re-form the gate map from the TSV per channel
(`plot.png` is the live monitor, not the measurement), with the device
card's channel arithmetic — including any mandatory gain division on the
current channel. Pull the dielectric-stack prior from the card and form
prior capacitances: `c = stack_capacitance([(t_nm, kappa), ...])` per
gate (series stacks — e.g. hBN over SiO₂ — are first-class).

**Step 1 — extract the CNP ridge, per channel.** For each four-terminal
channel separately (a 2T argmax is pulled off the CNP by contact features
and the V_bg≈0 stripe; never average channels — on a mosaic device the
channels disagree and the disagreement is signal, not noise): along each
gate-map row, locate the Rxx maximum across the fast axis. Smooth before
argmax when noisy (a 1D gaussian along the fast axis is the corpus
idiom). Three guards:
- **edge-clipped rows**: a row whose maximum sits at the swept-window
  edge has not located the CNP — exclude it from the fit and report the
  surviving row coverage; many clipped rows means the map is inadequate
  (see When).
- **competing maxima**: away from the CNP, contact-driven features or
  secondary peaks can outrun the CNP maximum. Restrict the argmax to a
  window around the visually-continuous ridge, or enforce continuity
  row-to-row; a ridge that jumps discontinuously is two features, not
  one line.
- **railed / glitch rows**: a 4T channel can rail at its sensitivity
  ceiling along a gapped CNP, flat-topping the argmax. Fit robustly —
  iterative outlier rejection (drop rows >~2σ off the line and refit)
  recovers the slope from the surviving rows; report the surviving
  coverage.

**Step 2 — fit, per channel.** Linear fit (`np.polyfit`) of ridge
position vs row coordinate; report slope and intercept per channel with
fit residuals. **State the axis orientation with the fit**: the
`c_bg/c_tg = −slope` reading in step 3 assumes the ridge position is
V_tg (fast axis) fitted against V_bg rows — a transposed map yields the
*inverted* ratio (e.g. 1.3 ↔ 0.77) with no other symptom until the
Verify geometry check; name which gate was which axis in the write-back. Read the residuals before trusting the line: structured
curvature (quantum capacitance, screening nonlinearity) makes a linear
slope window-dependent — if present, fit over the operating window the
campaign will actually use and say so. Cross-channel check: slopes
agreeing to a few percent → one calibration for the device *(heuristic
threshold — n = 1 device to date; better: compare the disagreement
against the per-channel fit residuals and say which bound you used)*;
disagreement beyond that is real spatial variation — keep per-channel
calibrations, flag it, and carry the channel question forward (it feeds
channel triage in the stacking/feature recipes; this recipe records the
disagreement, it does not interpret it).

**Step 3 — update the conversion.** From the chosen fit:
- **ratio**: `c_bg/c_tg = −slope`. Hold the better-constrained gate's
  capacitance at its stack prior and set the other from the ratio
  (heuristic — usually the simple single-dielectric gate is the anchor;
  state which you anchored).
- **density offset**: choose `n_offset` so the fitted line maps to
  n = 0: with `b` the V_tg intercept at V_bg = 0,
  `n_offset = -calc_nD(b, 0, c_tg, c_bg)[0]`.
- **D offset**: leave 0 unless the device exhibits a feature that
  physically locates D = 0 (e.g. a symmetric response in ±D); if you
  set it, cite the feature. An unexamined D_offset = 0 is itself a
  stated assumption — say it.
- **closure check**: `calc_nD` along the fitted ridge must return
  n ≈ 0; quote the max |n| residual as the calibration quality number.

**Step 4 — design constant-D lines.** Generate gate vectors with
`calc_gate_voltages(ns, D0*ones, c_tg, c_bg, n_offset=...)` and **clip
to the committed validators by dropping out-of-range points, not
clamping them** (clamping bends the line in (n, D); dropping shortens
it). Report the *realized* n-window per D after clipping — at large |D|
it can be much narrower than requested, and a fan designed to the
requested window would silently lose rows. Design-time guards per STYLE
rule 12: point density along n sized to the finest expected feature,
stated in the proposing cell. Any run executed under this recipe (a
confirmation cut along a designed line) tags
`s.add_comment('cnp-and-dline-calibration')`.

**Step 5 — write back.** Device card gets: per-channel slope/intercept
(+ run id of the source map), chosen (c_tg, c_bg) with the two-tier
provenance, offsets, residual quality, realized D-line table, and the
explicit upgrade path: *absolute scale pending quantum-Hall lever-arm
check* — when field data exists, ray slopes must quantize
(dn/dB = ν·e/h); a non-integer Δν spacing means the scale is wrong and
every ν claim inherits the error (recalibrate before classifying).

## Verify
- **Roundtrip**: designed D-line vectors → `calc_nD` → D constant to
  numerical precision and n monotonic across the realized window.
- **Overlay**: fitted line drawn over the re-formed per-channel map —
  the ridge and the fit must track by eye; a fit that misses the ridge
  passed the math and failed the extraction (step 1 guards).
- **Geometry sanity**: compare the fitted ratio against the stack
  prior's ratio; agreement is confirmation, disagreement at the tens-of-
  percent level means a wrong thickness/κ in the card or a wrong gate
  assignment in the map axes — resolve before writing back.
- **Lever-arm upgrade** (when field data exists): the step-5 check.

## Examples
- `vti/qingrui/20260601-QC0426-3LGr` *(our-measurement)* — the worked
  chain this recipe encodes. Measure cells 81–88: the 0 T TG–BG
  megasweep pair (197-pt back-gate rows). Analysis cells 10–11: the
  per-row argmax + `polyfit` extraction, cell 11 adding
  `gaussian_filter1d` smoothing — yielding `Vtg = −1.3·Vbg + 0.06`
  per the Rxx channels. Analysis cell 15: `sanitize_tg_bg`, the
  clip-by-dropping D-line designer this recipe's step 4 generalizes.
  Analysis cell 24: the inline capacitance `calc_nD` (t_tg = 15.6 nm,
  t_bg = 12 nm, κ_hBN = 3) — now canonical in `sharpelab_nb.gates`; on
  this device the geometry ratio (15.6/12 = 1.3) and the fitted slope
  agreed exactly, the happy case of the Verify geometry-sanity check.
  The campaign's D-line offset table (line constant ≈ −8·D) is device
  card content, consumed by the fan-design cells (analysis 50/58/61).
- Toploader corpus *(citation)*: `gatemap.md` defers CNP extraction to
  a then-unwritten recipe, and `landau-fan.md` names an SdH-frequency
  `cap-ratio-calibration` (still deferred) as the independent
  cross-method. This recipe is the CNP-slope method; the SdH method,
  when written, refines the same (c_tg, c_bg) from fan data and slots
  into step 5's upgrade path.

## Next
- Default: the campaign's first designed measurement — the D-lines feed
  `landau-fan` fast axes and `nD-map` polygons; the realized-window
  table from step 4 is the input to their wall-clock pricing.
- Quantum-Hall data lands: run the lever-arm check (step 5); on failure,
  recalibrate and re-emit the D-line table before any ν assignment.
- Per-channel slopes disagree: carry the per-channel calibrations into
  the campaign's channel-triage step (`trilayer-stacking-id` step 2 or
  equivalent); do not average them away.
- CNP clipped or absent in the map: extend the `gatemap` window (or
  revisit `silicon-backgate-survey` — a screening-gate operating point
  can move the CNP into reach), then re-enter at step 1.

# A lock-in measurement column is the in-phase X reading; its companion
# `_P` (phase) column is not part of the gain model.
_X_COL_RE = re.compile(r"_X$")
# Trailing integer of a channel id keys the mc gain/label: 'sr0' -> 0,
# 'sr830_1' -> 1 (so columns sr0_X and sr830_1_X both map correctly).
_TRAILING_INT_RE = re.compile(r"(\d+)(?!.*\d)")
# A channel is treated as a (transimpedance) current channel — reported in
# amps rather than converted to resistance — if its gain is negative, large
# in magnitude, or its mc label mentions current.
_CURRENT_GAIN_MAG = 1e4


@dataclass
class Channel:
    """One lock-in channel resolved from metadata."""

    col: str          # column name in the TSV, e.g. 'sr0_X'
    idx: int          # column index into the data matrix
    cid: str          # channel id without _X, e.g. 'sr0' / 'sr830_1'
    n: int            # trailing-integer channel index (mc key 'sr{n}')
    gain: float       # measurement_config gain (1.0 if absent)
    label: str        # mc role string, e.g. 'drain current on 42' / '09-01'
    is_current: bool  # report as current (else resistance/voltage)


def _as_float(v: Any) -> float | None:
    try:
        return float(v)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None


def _channel_index(cid: str) -> int | None:
    m = _TRAILING_INT_RE.search(cid)
    return int(m.group(1)) if m else None


def resolve_channels(meta: dict[str, Any], include: list[str] | None = None) -> list[Channel]:
    """Resolve the lock-in `_X` columns of a run into `Channel`s.

    Gains and role labels come from `meta['measurement_config']`. `include`,
    if given, restricts to those channel ids (e.g. ['sr1','sr2']) or column
    names. Handles both rig namings (`sr0_X`↔`sr0_gain`, `sr830_1_X`↔`sr1_gain`).
    """
    cols = list(meta.get("columns") or [])
    mc = meta.get("measurement_config") or {}
    want = set(include) if include else None
    channels: list[Channel] = []
    for idx, col in enumerate(cols):
        if not _X_COL_RE.search(col):
            continue
        cid = _X_COL_RE.sub("", col)
        if want is not None and cid not in want and col not in want:
            continue
        n = _channel_index(cid)
        gain = None
        if f"{cid}_gain" in mc:
            gain = _as_float(mc[f"{cid}_gain"])
        elif n is not None and f"sr{n}_gain" in mc:
            gain = _as_float(mc[f"sr{n}_gain"])
        if gain is None or gain == 0.0:
            gain = 1.0
        label = ""
        if n is not None and isinstance(mc.get(f"sr{n}"), str):
            label = mc[f"sr{n}"]
        elif isinstance(mc.get(cid), str):
            label = mc[cid]
        is_current = gain < 0 or abs(gain) >= _CURRENT_GAIN_MAG or "current" in label.lower()
        channels.append(
            Channel(col=col, idx=idx, cid=cid, n=n if n is not None else -1,
                    gain=gain, label=label, is_current=is_current)
        )
    return channels


def current_channel(channels: list[Channel]) -> Channel | None:
    """The single transimpedance current channel, or None if not exactly one.

    The measured drain current (gain-divided) is the denominator of the
    four-probe resistance R = V / I — see `resistance_grids`.
    """
    currents = [c for c in channels if c.is_current]
    return currents[0] if len(currents) == 1 else None


@dataclass
class Run:
    """A loaded sweep run."""

    path: Path
    meta: dict[str, Any]
    cols: list[str]
    data: np.ndarray  # (rows, ncols), float

    def col(self, name: str) -> np.ndarray:
        """Column named `name` as a 1-D array.

        A duplicated name (a swept param that is also followed writes the
        planned setpoint AND the readback under one name) resolves to the
        first occurrence — the planned/setpoint instance, matching
        `summarize_run` and `FanGrids.grid` — with a warning naming every
        index; `col_at(idx)` selects the others. Raises KeyError if absent.
        """
        idxs = self.col_indices(name)
        if not idxs:
            raise KeyError(f"no column named {name!r}; cols: {self.cols}")
        if len(idxs) > 1:
            warnings.warn(
                f"column {name!r} appears at indices {idxs}; returning index "
                f"{idxs[0]} (the planned/setpoint instance) — col_at(idx) "
                "selects the others",
                stacklevel=2,
            )
        return self.data[:, idxs[0]]

    def col_at(self, idx: int) -> np.ndarray:
        return self.data[:, idx]

    def col_indices(self, name: str) -> list[int]:
        return [i for i, c in enumerate(self.cols) if c == name]

    @property
    def metadata(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Alias for `meta` (the parsed `metadata.json`). The on-disk file,
        the docstrings, and the sweep ecosystem (`w.metadata`,
        `sweep_load.load_meta`) all use 'metadata' — both names resolve here."""
        return self.meta

    @property
    def recipe(self) -> str | None:
        """The recipe slug, conventionally the first metadata comment."""
        comments = self.meta.get("comments") or []
        return comments[0] if comments else None

    @property
    def tags(self) -> list[str]:
        """Comments after the recipe slug (e.g. 'gate: tg')."""
        comments = self.meta.get("comments") or []
        return list(comments[1:])

    @property
    def swept_axis(self) -> str | None:
        """For 1D sweeps, metadata['param']."""
        return self.meta.get("param")

    @property
    def setpoints(self) -> list[float] | None:
        sp = self.meta.get("setpoints")
        return list(sp) if sp is not None else None

    @property
    def interrupted(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.meta.get("interrupted", False))

    @property
    def complete(self) -> bool:
        """True once sweep has finalized the run (`end_time` lands in
        metadata at close; the interrupt flag also finalizes). An in-flight
        run has neither."""
        return self.meta.get("end_time") is not None or self.interrupted

    @property
    def kind(self) -> str | None:
        return self.meta.get("type")

    @property
    def rows(self) -> int:
        return int(self.data.shape[0])


def open_run(path: str | Path) -> Run:
    """Open a sweep run directory — completed or in flight.

    `path` is the run dir (e.g. `<notebook>/data/119`). Must contain
    `metadata.json` and either `data.tsv.gz` or `data.tsv`. Column names
    come from metadata — TSVs are headerless, and sweep writes `columns`
    to `metadata.json` at sweep start, so names resolve mid-run too. An
    in-flight run's TSV may end mid-row; only newline-terminated rows are
    trusted (sweep writes row-at-a-time, so interior lines are whole).
    """
    path = Path(path).expanduser().resolve()
    if not path.is_dir():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"not a directory: {path}")

    meta_path = path / "metadata.json"
    if not meta_path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"missing metadata.json in {path}")
    meta = json.loads(meta_path.read_text())

    cols = list(meta.get("columns") or [])
    if not cols:
        raise ValueError(f"metadata.json has no 'columns' entry in {path}")

    tsv_gz = path / "data.tsv.gz"
    tsv = path / "data.tsv"
    if tsv_gz.exists():
        raw = gzip.decompress(tsv_gz.read_bytes())
    elif tsv.exists():
        raw = tsv.read_bytes()
    else:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no data.tsv(.gz) in {path}")

def fan_grids(run: "str | Path | Run", columns: list[str] | None = None) -> FanGrids:
    """Re-form a 2D fan into per-column grids, keeping only complete slow rows.

    `run` is a run directory or an already-loaded `Run`. `nfast` comes from
    metadata (never hardcoded); trailing rows of an in-progress sweep are
    dropped via `nrows = total // nfast`. `columns` restricts which columns
    are retained in `.data`/`.cols` (the reshape is unaffected).
    """
    r = run if isinstance(run, Run) else open_run(run)
    nfast = _fast_count(r.meta)
    nrows = r.data.shape[0] // nfast
    data = r.data[: nrows * nfast]
    cols = r.cols
    if columns is not None:
        keep = [r.cols.index(c) for c in columns]
        data = data[:, keep]
        cols = list(columns)
    return FanGrids(nrows=nrows, nfast=nfast, cols=cols, data=data,
                    meta=r.meta, slow_param=_slow_param(r.meta))


@dataclass
class ResistanceGrids:
    """Gain-applied four-probe resistances, using the measured current."""

    current: np.ndarray            # I grid (nrows, nfast), amps
    current_channel: str           # cid of the transimpedance channel
    R: dict[str, np.ndarray]       # voltage cid -> signed R grid (Ω)


def resistance_grids(fan: FanGrids, channels: list[str] | None = None) -> ResistanceGrids:
    """Per-channel resistance grids `R = (V/gain_V) / I` from a `FanGrids`.

    The denominator is the *measured* drain current `I = X_cur / gain_cur`
    (a grid — it sags where the device is resistive), not a nominal bias
    current. Gains come from `measurement_config` (shared `resolve_channels`);
    nothing is hardcoded. Returned R is **signed** (X/I) — take `np.abs` for
    Rxx magnitude, keep the sign for Rxy/Hall. `channels` restricts the
    voltage channels returned (the current channel is always resolved).
    """
    all_chans = resolve_channels(fan.meta)
    cur = current_channel(all_chans)
    if cur is None:
        n_cur = sum(c.is_current for c in all_chans)
        raise ValueError(
            f"need exactly one current channel to form resistance; found {n_cur}. "
            "Pass it via measurement_config gains (transimpedance gain is negative "
            "or |gain| >= 1e4)."
        )
    want = set(channels) if channels else None
    I = fan.grid(cur.col) / cur.gain
    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
        R = {
            v.cid: (fan.grid(v.col) / v.gain) / I
            for v in all_chans
            if not v.is_current and (want is None or v.cid in want or v.col in want)
        }
    return ResistanceGrids(current=I, current_channel=cur.cid, R=R)

class SdhTone:
    """One SdH tone's onset track from the matched-filter walk.

    `snr`/`amp` are per-window curves over `b_centers` (high-B → low-B). The
    filter is a Gaussian-windowed complex correlation at fixed `freq` whose
    FWHM spans `n_periods` periods of that tone (support `win_invB` in 1/B);
    SNR is amplitude over the record's white-noise floor, so a light tone and
    a heavy tone are each judged in their own natural window.
    """

    freq: float               # tone frequency, Tesla (record-resolution FFT)
    contrast: float           # tone-ID peak over the record spectral floor
    onset_b: float            # low-B onset, Tesla (record low edge if censored)
    censored: bool            # still above threshold in the lowest window
    revived: bool             # above-threshold windows exist below the walk stop
    marginal: bool            # peak SNR < marginal_mult x threshold everywhere
    near_residual: bool       # filter passband overlaps the detrend-residual band
    n_periods: float          # filter FWHM in periods (shrunk if record short)
    win_invB: float           # filter support width, 1/T
    harmonic_of: float | None  # freq of the lower tone this sits at ~k x of (fund.)
    harmonics: tuple[float, ...]  # freqs of tones that sit at ~k x of this one
    b_centers: np.ndarray     # per-window center field, descending (n_win,)
    snr: np.ndarray           # matched-filter SNR per window (n_win,)
    amp: np.ndarray           # matched-filter amplitude per window, Ohm-units

    def delta_f(self, b_max: float) -> float:
        """FFT resolution δF = 1/(1/onset_b − 1/b_max) over this tone's usable
        record — the per-tone version of the landau-fan design number."""
        return 1.0 / (1.0 / self.onset_b - 1.0 / b_max)


@dataclass
class SdhOnset:
    """Per-tone SdH onsets over the usable field window.

    `onset_b` is the headline: the lowest onset over non-marginal tracked
    tones — the low-B edge of usable oscillation content, which is the
    `landau-fan` step-1 `B_lo` contract (a light tone alive below the dominant
    tone's edge carries it). Everything behind it is in `tones` (per-tone
    onsets, SNR curves, censored/revived/marginal flags) and `untracked`
    (tones seen in the record-wide FFT but not trackable, with reasons).
    `summary()` renders the whole read for a notebook cell.
    """

    onset_b: float                       # min onset over robust tones, Tesla
    onset_freq: float                    # freq of the tone carrying onset_b
    clip_high_b: float                   # high edge of the analyzed window
    b_lo_record: float                   # low-B edge of the analyzed record
    noise_sigma: float                   # per-sample white-noise sigma used
    tones: list[SdhTone]                 # tracked tones, by contrast desc
    untracked: list[tuple[float, str]]   # (freq, reason) for untrackable tones

    @property
    def consensus_freq(self) -> float:
        """Dominant (highest-contrast) tone frequency, Tesla."""
        return self.tones[0].freq

    @property
    def b_centers(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """Dominant tone's window centers (see `tones` for the rest)."""
        return self.tones[0].b_centers

    @property
    def snr(self) -> np.ndarray:
        """Dominant tone's SNR curve (see `tones` for the rest)."""
        return self.tones[0].snr

    def summary(self) -> str:
        """Multi-line read for a notebook cell: headline, per-tone table,
        untracked tones with reasons."""
        carrier = f"tone {self.onset_freq:.1f} T"
        lines = [
            f"sdh_onset: onset_b = {self.onset_b:.2f} T ({carrier}) over "
            f"B [{self.b_lo_record:.2f}, {self.clip_high_b:.2f}] T"
        ]
        for t in self.tones:
            flags = [f for f, on in (("censored@edge", t.censored),
                                     ("revives-below-gap", t.revived),
                                     ("marginal", t.marginal),
                                     ("near-residual", t.near_residual)) if on]
            if t.harmonic_of is not None:
                k = t.freq / t.harmonic_of
                flags.append(f"~{k:.0f}x{t.harmonic_of:.1f}T")
            for fh in t.harmonics:
                flags.append(f"{round(fh / t.freq):.0f}x->{fh:.1f}T")
            tag = f"  [{', '.join(flags)}]" if flags else ""
            lines.append(
                f"  tone {t.freq:6.1f} T: onset {t.onset_b:5.2f} T  "
                f"dF {t.delta_f(self.clip_high_b):5.2f} T  "
                f"snr_max {np.nanmax(t.snr):6.1f}{tag}"
            )
        for f_t, reason in self.untracked:
            lines.append(f"  tone {f_t:6.1f} T: UNTRACKED — {reason}")
        return "\n".join(lines)

def sdh_fft(
    R_grid: np.ndarray,
    B: np.ndarray,
    *,
    b_range: tuple[float, float] | None = None,
    nfft: int = 512,
    bg_degree: int | None = 5,
    window: str | None = "hann",
    log: bool = True,
    floor: float = 1.0,
    uniform_rtol: float = 0.1,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Per-column Shubnikov–de Haas FFT in 1/B.

    `R_grid` is `(n_B, n_fast)` (rows = field, the `FanGrids` row axis); `B`
    is the per-row field `(n_B,)` — arbitrarily spaced. For each column:
    select `b_range`, optionally `log10(max(R, floor))`, remove a degree-
    `bg_degree` polynomial background in **B-space** (`None` skips), then take
    the FFT in 1/B. The background subtraction happens on the raw B axis
    *before* the 1/B step because the MR background is smooth in B, not 1/B.

    The 1/B resample is **conditional**. The field may be swept uniformly in
    1/B (then the samples are already evenly spaced in 1/B and are FFT'd
    directly, zero-padded to `nfft`) or uniformly in B (then the 1/B samples
    are resampled onto a regular `nfft`-point grid by interpolation against
    **sorted** 1/B). Which path is taken is decided from the actual 1/B
    spacing distribution (`uniform_rtol`), not an assumed step.

    Returns `(freqs, spec)` — `freqs` in Tesla `(n_freq,)`, `spec` the FFT
    magnitude `(n_fast, n_freq)`.
    """
    B = np.asarray(B, dtype=float)
    R_grid = np.asarray(R_grid, dtype=float)
    if R_grid.shape[0] != B.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError(f"R_grid rows {R_grid.shape[0]} != len(B) {B.shape[0]}")
    sel = np.ones(B.shape, dtype=bool) if b_range is None else (B >= b_range[0]) & (B <= b_range[1])
    if sel.sum() < 4:
        raise ValueError(f"need >=4 field rows in b_range; got {int(sel.sum())}")
    Bsel = B[sel]
    invB = 1.0 / Bsel
    order = np.argsort(invB)
    invB_sorted = invB[order]

    uniform = _is_uniform(invB_sorted, uniform_rtol)
    if uniform:
        m = invB_sorted.size
        du = (invB_sorted[-1] - invB_sorted[0]) / (m - 1)
        nout = max(nfft, m)
        win = _window(window, m)
    else:
        u = np.linspace(invB_sorted[0], invB_sorted[-1], nfft)
        du = u[1] - u[0]
        nout = nfft
        win = _window(window, nfft)
    freqs = np.fft.rfftfreq(nout, du)  # Tesla

    spec = np.zeros((R_grid.shape[1], freqs.size))
    for j in range(R_grid.shape[1]):
        y = R_grid[sel, j]
        if log:
            y = np.log10(np.maximum(y, floor))
        if bg_degree is not None:
            y = _bg_subtract_B(Bsel, y, bg_degree)
        ys = y[order]
        if uniform:
            spec[j] = np.abs(np.fft.rfft(ys * win, n=nout))
        else:
            yi = np.interp(u, invB_sorted, ys)
            spec[j] = np.abs(np.fft.rfft(yi * win))
    return freqs, spec

def sdh_onset(
    R: np.ndarray,
    B: np.ndarray,
    *,
    b_hi: float | None = None,
    b_lo: float = 0.3,
    r_full_scale: float | None = None,
    headroom: float = 0.95,
    bg_degree: int = 5,
    f_min: float = 3.0,
    snr_threshold: float = 5.0,
    n_periods: float = 3.0,
    min_periods: float = 2.0,
    step_frac: float = 0.25,
    gap_widths: float = 0.5,
    min_pts: int = 8,
    max_tones: int = 8,
    tone_floor_mult: float = 4.0,
    marginal_mult: float = 2.0,

    """Per-tone low-B onsets of the SdH oscillations in a single Rxx trace.

    `R` is one longitudinal-resistance trace `(n_B,)`, `B` the matching field
    `(n_B,)` (arbitrary spacing). Removes a degree-`bg_degree` B-space
    polynomial background, identifies every SdH tone via nested high-B FFT
    scans (`_tone_id`), then walks each tone's Gaussian matched filter from
    high B down to where it sinks into the record's white-noise floor
    (`_track_tone` — a 5σ-style statistical onset, which legitimately sits
    below a by-eye read).

    Returns an `SdhOnset`; `onset_b` is the minimum onset over non-marginal
    tones — the `B_lo` a `landau-fan` design should use, correct even when a
    light tone outlives the dominant tone (per-dominant-tone semantics
    silently mis-served light-tone hunts). A tone still above threshold in
    its lowest window is *censored*: its onset is the record's low edge and a
    warning notes oscillations persist to the end of the record.

    If `r_full_scale` is given (sensitivity / I_bias, Ohms), samples at
    ≥ `headroom` x full scale soft-clip: the analysis window is truncated
    below the lowest clipped field, `clip_high_b` reports the truncation, and
    a warning fires. Without it no clip detection is attempted.

    Failure is never a nan: raises `SdhOnsetError` (record too short, no tones
    above the spectral floor, or no identified tone trackable), with the scan
    diagnostics in the message. Partial failures warn and land in
    `SdhOnset.untracked`.
    """
    B = np.asarray(B, dtype=float)
    R = np.asarray(R, dtype=float)
    if R.shape != B.shape:
        raise ValueError(f"R shape {R.shape} != B shape {B.shape}")
    b_hi = float(np.nanmax(B)) if b_hi is None else float(b_hi)

    if r_full_scale is not None:
        clipped = np.abs(R) >= headroom * r_full_scale
        if clipped.any():
            b_clip = float(B[clipped].min())
            warnings.warn(
                f"sdh_onset: |R| reaches {float(np.abs(R).max()):.3g} Ω vs "
                f"full scale {r_full_scale:g} Ω (soft clip, ≥{headroom:g}x "
                f"from B = {b_clip:.2f} T); analysis window truncated to "
                f"{b_clip:.2f} T",
                stacklevel=2,
            )
            b_hi = min(b_hi, b_clip)

    sel = (B >= b_lo) & (B <= b_hi)
    Bs, Rs = B[sel], R[sel]
    if Bs.size < min_pts:
        raise SdhOnsetError(
            f"need >={min_pts} field rows in [{b_lo:g}, {b_hi:g}] T; got {Bs.size}"
        )
    bg = _bg_subtract_B(Bs, Rs, bg_degree)
    invB = 1.0 / Bs
    order = np.argsort(invB)
    invB, bg = invB[order], bg[order]
    b_lo_record = float(1.0 / invB[-1])

    tones, diags = _tone_id(invB, bg, f_min, tone_floor_mult, max_tones,
                            min_pts, n_periods)
    if not tones:
        raise SdhOnsetError(
            f"no SdH tones above {tone_floor_mult:g}x the spectral floor in "
            f"B [{b_lo_record:.2f}, {Bs.max():.2f}] T — nested scans: "
            + "; ".join(diags)
        )

    sigma = _noise_sigma(bg)
    f_resid = max(f_min, 5.0 / (invB[-1] - invB[0]))  # detrend-residual band edge
    tracks: list[SdhTone] = []
    untracked: list[tuple[float, str]] = []
    for f_t, contrast, harm, harms in tones:
        tr, reason = _track_tone(
            invB, bg, f_t, sigma, n_periods=n_periods, min_periods=min_periods,
            step_frac=step_frac, min_pts=min_pts, snr_threshold=snr_threshold,
            gap_widths=gap_widths, marginal_mult=marginal_mult,
        )
        if tr is None:

        tracks.append(SdhTone(

            censored=tr["censored"], revived=tr["revived"],
            marginal=tr["marginal"],
            near_residual=bool(f_t - 2.0 * sigma_f < f_resid),
            n_periods=tr["n_periods"],

    if not tracks:

            "tones found but none trackable: "
            + "; ".join(f"{f:.1f} T — {r}" for f, r in untracked)

    if untracked:

        and any(o.harmonic_of == t.freq and o.contrast < t.contrast for o in tracks)

    robust = [t for t in tracks if not t.marginal
              and (not t.near_residual or t.freq in corroborated)]
    pool = robust if robust else tracks
    carrier = min(pool, key=lambda t: t.onset_b)
    if robust:
        overall_min = min(tracks, key=lambda t: t.onset_b)
        if overall_min.onset_b < carrier.onset_b:

## Burn log

1. **2026-06-11, QC0426 live session** (`trilayer-stacking-id`): the
   step-4 rule "crossings at finite D no longer count as ABA evidence"
   — written conservatively to prevent overconfidence — caused HERA to
   discard the chain hunt at D = +0.25 entirely ("this run informs gap
   physics, not the chain hunt"). The physics: crossing *presence* at
   finite D is indeed not ABA evidence (Lee et al.), but a chain
   *pattern* matching the ML×BL model loci still is, weakening with
   |D|. Fixed by restating per rules 1–2. Lesson: rounding a
   conditional rule toward caution miscalibrates exactly as badly as
   rounding it toward confidence.

2. **2026-06-10/11, QC0426 live session** (`landau-fan` +
   session brief): iteration-1 fan was B-axis aliased (0.25 T rows vs
   ~0.29 T in-window SdH period) — blocky texture, arc evidence
   discounted; recovered by the overnight 0.05 T fan. Failure chain
   spanned three documents: the brief carried a toploader-derived
   "~30 s/row" (measured: 278 s/row, ramp-limited on a blocking
   magnet), the agent sized a coarse-B fan to the mispriced budget, and
   no design-time Nyquist guard existed to catch it. Fixed by the
   landau-fan grid-design check + full cost model and rules 11–12.
   Lesson: a wrong constant with false authority plus a missing design
   guard compound; agnostic recipes with instrument-class conditionals
   force the agent to resolve parameters against the actual rig.

3. **2026-06-10, QC0426 live session** (run-5 SdH-FFT analysis): three
   successive f_low-extraction schemes gave conflicting slope signs
   before the agent stepped back and separated robust findings (two
   frequency scales, f₁+f₂=f_tot) from window-dependent ones (f_low's
   n-dependence). The agent self-diagnosed the spiral in its session
   notes; rule 14 canonizes its own lesson. Lesson: refinement loops on
   extraction-sensitive quantities consume session time and manufacture
   confidence — the fork report + deciding measurement is the correct
   terminal state.

4. **2026-06-10/11, QC0426 live session** (`trilayer-stacking-id`,
   post-mortem 06-12): run-4's vertical candidate came from a 4-row /
   0.25 T window — a dispersing minimum (true slope-ν ≈ 5.1 at fine
   rows) read as "non-dispersing". No rule barred a dispersion claim
   from a window that cannot resolve dispersion; the session
   adjudicated it correctly (anomaly, not evidence) but retiring the
   candidate cost a queued measurement. Fixed by the step-3 dispersion
   floor (≥ ~8 B-rows spanning ≥ 1.5 T, else "dispersion
   undetermined"). Lesson: a classifier without a stated resolution
   floor manufactures candidates from coarse data.

5. **2026-06-10, QC0426 live session** (round-2 device card + brief): an
   operating setpoint — Si = +50 V — quoted in an agent-visible file was
   inherited verbatim as the screening default rather than chosen or
   re-derived; the provenance trace shows it propagating as a choice the
   agent never made. Recurred 2026-06-14 in the same class — "round 2" /
   "replication" framing baked into the deployed templates built to fix
   this very leak (the campaign frame is itself an operational default).
   Fixed by rule 11's setpoint exception and the blinding conventions
   (`hera/blinding.md`). Lesson: operational defaults are information; an
   agent-visible file that quotes one makes the choice for the agent.

6. **2026-06-14, QC0426 live session** (`contact-survey-2t` + measure
   kit): the survey dwell was set to a round `SURVEY_DELAY = 0.5 s` to
   match the scout, not derived from the lock-in time constant; the
   SR830 τ was front-panel-set, unset by the kit, and stored `None` in
   run metadata, so the dwell-vs-τ relationship was implicit and
   unchecked (operator flagged it). Fixed by rule 12's settling floor +
   the VTI rig-card lock-in note + a bring-up τ-record step. Lesson:
   derive the dwell from the measured τ rather than a round number; the
   floor can be bent knowingly on a smooth signal, but an unexamined
   dwell on an unknown τ is a latent bias no later analysis can audit.

7. **2026-06-19, QC0426 .3 session** (`landau-fan` step 1): the electron
   fan's fixed sensitivity (1e-5) was sized for the metallic SdH region off
   the spot-check R-scale (n = 5e12, ≤ 171 Ω); the fan reached n = 1e12 where
   R ∝ 1/n × MR rails > 550 Ω, clipping 17% of the map — the n ≲ 2e12 high-B
   region, i.e. the bottom of the labeling band the fan exists to resolve.
   HERA predicted the clip and accepted it as an amplitude trade,
   mis-scoping the expendable region. Fixed by the step-1 worst-corner
   dynamic-range guard + the clipping-vs-streak Next item. Lesson: a
   fixed-sens 2D fan sizes to R(n_min, B_max), not the metallic region;
   clipping is FFT-distorting, and the design-time dynamic-range guard (rule
   12) is the sibling of the Nyquist guard (burn #2) — omitting it fails the
   same way.

8. **2026-06-19, QC0426 .3 session** (`landau-fan` fast_delay): the fan's
   fast-axis dwell was shaved as a benign "amplitude-for-time" trade, on the
   rule-12 license that a uniform lag only shifts an intercept. But the fast
   axis feeds a per-column FFT, where the lag suppresses the high-frequency
   tones — it gutted the stacking discriminator the fan existed to read, and
   only the full-settling spot checks carried it. Severity scaled with the
   coarse n-sampling, not the dwell alone. Fixed by rule-12's fast-axis
   carve-out + the step-7 note. Lesson: the intercept-only license is for 1D
   slope extraction; on a fan's fast axis under-settling costs the high-F
   tones, and density — not just dwell — buys it back.

9. **2026-07-14.2 → 16, QC0426 VTI sessions** (`trilayer-stacking-fs-count`
   + `landau-fan` + brief): the FS-count model's numerical clamp
   (|n| ≤ 3.5e12, electron-only) had been quoted onto agent-visible
   surfaces as "validity", and the agent designed *acquisition* to it —
   spot checks at the clamp, a hole-side fan stopped at −3.5e12 with the
   gate range reaching ±6.4e12 — halving the fan's usable record and
   leaving the top tone unresolved; the density/side choices also defeated
   the overlay the clamp belonged to. PI review traced four complaints to
   this one root. Fixed by the quote deletions + model extension
   (2026-07-18) and rule 17. Lesson: a tool limit written where the agent
   can read it becomes a design constraint; the window clips the claim,
   not the sweep.

# `sweep` (measureme) API Reference

The measurement layer: `lib/measureme`, imported as `import sweep`. A
`Station` collects QCoDeS parameters to follow, runs 0D–2D sweeps, and writes
each run to a directory (`data.tsv.gz` + `metadata.json`) via a `Writer`.

Source: `sweep/sweep.py`, `sweep/db.py`. `import sweep` re-exports the
`sweep.sweep` surface (`from .sweep import *`); `sweep.db`, `sweep.raster`,
`sweep.sweep_load` are submodules.

---

## Station

### `Station(measurement_config=None, basedir=None, verbose=True)`
A collection of followed parameters with sweep methods. `measurement_config`
is an arbitrary dict stamped into every run's `metadata.json` (channel→contact,
gains, bias, …). `basedir` is the run-directory root; falls back to the module
`BASEDIR` (see `set_basedir`) then `os.getcwd()`. The station writes `log.log`
into `basedir`, so the directory must exist before construction.

### `AsyncStation(measurement_config=None, basedir=None, verbose=True)`
Subclass of `Station`, same constructor and identical I/O / data layout. Reads
are parallelized per-instrument (one thread per distinct instrument, one
executor reused across a sweep), and same-instrument parameters are
batch-read when supported — SR830 `snap` (`SnapReadable`, ≤6 params) or
SR86x `get_values` (`BatchReadable`, ≤3 params), else sequential. Use this by
default; it produces byte-identical output to `Station`.

### `follow_param(param, gain=1.0)` → `Station` · alias **`fp`**
Append a QCoDeS parameter to the followed list. The stored column value is
**`param() / gain`** (gain division happens at read time). Returns the station,
so calls chain: `s.fp(sr0.X, gain).fp(sr0.P)`. For a true-current channel
follow it with `gain=1`. Column name is `param.full_name`.

### `add_comment(comment)`
Append a comment to `metadata['comments']`. **Comments are station-lifetime**:
every comment added since construction lands in every subsequent run's
metadata — rebuild (or otherwise reset) the station between runs of different
intent. `metadata['comments'][0]` is conventionally the recipe slug.

### `ramp(param, setpoint)`
Logged direct set — calls `param(setpoint)`. It does **not** sub-step; smooth
ramping is the driver's own `step`/`inter_delay` (or a driver `ramp_*` method).

### `register_run_before(fn, args)` / `register_run_after(fn, args)`
Register a hook called at each measured point. `args` must be a tuple. The hook
is called `fn(*args, **context)` where **context is injected by parameter
name** (via `inspect.signature` — the hook receives only the context keys it
declares):

| context key | available in | value |
|---|---|---|
| `station` | before & after | the `Station` |
| `writer` | before & after | the active `sweep.db.Writer` |
| `data` | after only | the most recent data row (list) |

A hook whose parameter is named `station` gets it from context — passing it in
`args` too double-binds (`TypeError: multiple values for 'station'`). Order any
`args`-supplied params before the context ones. Keyword-only hook params can't
be set positionally via `args`; bind them with `functools.partial` (signature
is seen through the partial, so injection still works).

### Other methods
- `measure()` → `SweepResult` — single 0D point.
- `watch(delay=0.0, max_duration=None)` → `SweepResult` — repeat-measure over
  time until `max_duration` (or interrupt).
- `read(param, gain=1.0)` / `read_all()` — log a one-off read, no run written.
- `plot(x, y, z=None)` / `reset_plots()` — live monitor only, not the data.
- `reset()` — clear the interrupted flag so the station can sweep again.

---

## Sweeps

Each sweep method returns a `SweepResult` and writes one run directory. The
**data-row column layout** is fixed per method (and matches `metadata['columns']`).
`*followed` is the followed-parameter values in `fp` order, each already
gain-divided.

| method | signature | row layout |
|---|---|---|
| `measure` | `()` | `[time, *followed]` |
| `watch` | `(delay=0.0, max_duration=None)` | `[time, *followed]` |
| `sweep` | `(param, setpoints, delay=0.0)` | `[time, setpoint, *followed]` |
| `multisweep` | `(params, setpointslist, delay=0.0)` | `[time, *setpoints, *followed]` |
| `megasweep` | `(slow_param, slow_v, fast_param, fast_v, slow_delay=0.0, fast_delay=0.0, init_delay=True)` | `[time, slow, fast, *followed]` |
| `multimegasweep` | `(slow_params, slow_v_list, fast_params, fast_v_list, slow_delay=0.0, fast_delay=0.0, init_delay=True)` | `[time, *slow, *fast, *followed]` |

- **`sweep`** — 1D. Sets `param` to each setpoint, waits `delay`, measures.
- **`multisweep`** — 1D, several parameters **co-swept**. `params` and
  `setpointslist` are parallel lists; `setpointslist[i]` is the vector for
  `params[i]`, and **all vectors must be equal length** (raises otherwise). At
  point j every `params[i]` is set to `setpointslist[i][j]` — one path through
  N-space, not a grid (e.g. a fixed-D (Vtg, Vbg) line).
- **`megasweep`** — 2D grid: outer `slow_param` over `slow_v`, inner
  `fast_param` over `fast_v`. `slow_delay` waits once per slow row (at the first
  fast point), `fast_delay` waits at every point.
- **`multimegasweep`** — 2D grid where each axis is a **co-swept bundle**.
  `slow_params`/`slow_v_list` and `fast_params`/`fast_v_list` are parallel
  lists; per-axis all vectors must be equal length. The grid is
  `len(slow_v) × len(fast_v)`; at each grid point every slow param and every
  fast param is set together. Example — field-slow, (Vtg, Vbg)-line-fast:
  `s.multimegasweep([magnet.field], [B_vec], [k_tg.volt, k_bg.volt], [Vtgs, Vbgs], slow_delay=1, fast_delay=0.9)`.
- **`init_delay`** (2D only) — `True` applies `slow_delay` before the very
  first point; `False` skips it (the axis is already parked there).

All sweeps are SIGINT-interruptible: an interrupt finishes the current point,
sets `metadata['interrupted'] = True`, and marks the station interrupted (call
`reset()` or rebuild before the next sweep).

### `SweepResult` (dataclass)
`SweepResult(basedir, id, metadata, datapath)` — the run root, the integer run
id, the final `metadata` dict, and the on-disk `data.tsv.gz` path.

def plot_raw(run: "str | Path | Run", channels: list[str] | None = None):
    """Canonical raw view of a run — the first plot, before any derived read.

    Every lock-in channel, gain-divided, on the run's own axes: 1D as traces
    vs the swept axis; 2D (fan/megasweep) as one pcolormesh per channel over
    (fast index, slow value), complete rows only. Voltage channels plot as
    signed R = (V/gain)/I against the measured current when a transimpedance
    channel resolves, else as V/gain; the current channel plots as I. No log,
    no clipping, no background removal — rails, dead/flat channels, streaks,
    and drift are visible here and hidden by derived views. Returns the Figure.
    """
    r = run if isinstance(run, Run) else open_run(run)
    all_chans = resolve_channels(r.meta)
    chans = all_chans
    if channels is not None:
        want = set(channels)
        chans = [c for c in all_chans if c.cid in want or c.col in want]
    if not chans:
        raise ValueError("no lock-in channels resolved from measurement_config")
    cur = current_channel(all_chans)

    try:
        _fast_count(r.meta)
        is_2d = True
    except ValueError:
        is_2d = False

    def _series(values: np.ndarray, c: Channel, I: np.ndarray | None):
        if c.is_current:
            return values, f"{c.cid or c.col} I (A)"
        if I is not None:
            with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
                return values / I, f"{c.cid or c.col} R (Ω)"
        return values, f"{c.cid or c.col} V (V)"

    if is_2d:
        fan = fan_grids(r)
        if fan.nrows == 0:
            raise ValueError(f"run {r.path.name}: no complete slow rows yet")
        try:
            y, ylabel = fan.slow, fan.slow_param
        except KeyError:
            y, ylabel = np.arange(fan.nrows), "slow row"
        x = np.arange(fan.nfast)
        I = fan.grid(cur.col) / cur.gain if cur is not None else None
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(chans), figsize=(4.6 * len(chans), 4.2),
                                 sharey=True, squeeze=False)
        for ax, c in zip(axes[0], chans):
            z, zlabel = _series(fan.grid(c.col) / c.gain, c, I)
            pm = ax.pcolormesh(x, y, z, shading="auto")
            fig.colorbar(pm, ax=ax, label=zlabel)
            ax.set_title(c.cid or c.col)
            ax.set_xlabel("fast idx")
        axes[0][0].set_ylabel(ylabel or "slow")
    else:
        x, xlabel = np.arange(r.rows), "row"
        if r.swept_axis:
            idxs = r.col_indices(r.swept_axis)
            if idxs:
                x, xlabel = r.data[:, idxs[0]], r.swept_axis
        I = r.data[:, cur.idx] / cur.gain if cur is not None else None
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(chans), 1, figsize=(9, 2.4 * len(chans)),
                                 sharex=True, squeeze=False)
        for ax, c in zip(axes[:, 0], chans):
            yv, ylab = _series(r.data[:, c.idx] / c.gain, c, I)
            ax.plot(x, yv, lw=0.7)
            ax.set_ylabel(ylab)
        axes[-1][0].set_xlabel(xlabel)

    fig.suptitle(f"run {r.path.name} — raw ({r.recipe or 'no recipe tag'})")
    fig.tight_layout()
    return fig

from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.signal import find_peaks
from hera.analysis import open_run, resolve_channels, plot_raw, sdh_onset, sdh_fft, summarize_run

for rid, n in [(6, 3.2), (7, -1.2)]:
    r = open_run(Path('data') / str(rid))
    print(summarize_run(r))
    plot_raw(r); plt.show()  # Native TSV, signed R and measured drain current FIRST.
    channels = {c.cid: c for c in resolve_channels(r.meta)}
    I = r.col('sr0_X') / channels['sr0'].gain
    R = (r.col('sr1_X') / channels['sr1'].gain) / I
    B = r.col('magnet_field')
    print(f'Elapsed {np.ptp(r.col(\"time\"))/60:.2f} min; R {R.min():.2f}..{R.max():.2f} ohm; I {I.min()*1e9:.3f}..{I.max()*1e9:.3f} nA')
    print(f'T_sample {r.col(\"T_sample\").min():.3f}..{r.col(\"T_sample\").max():.3f} K; peak |TG/BG current| {np.max(abs(r.col(\"k_2400_tg_curr\")))*1e12:.1f}/{np.max(abs(r.col(\"k_2400_bg_curr\")))*1e12:.1f} pA')
    on = sdh_onset(R, B, r_full_scale=5000)
    print('Full-record onset (all flags retained):\\n' + on.summary())
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 4))
    if rid == 6:
        # Sensitivity check, not a replacement of the censored full-record result.
        # High-field MR is large; use the measured low-B record to isolate onset.
        for deg in (3, 5):
            local = sdh_onset(R, B, b_hi=4, bg_degree=deg, r_full_scale=5000)
            print(f'Low-field-only onset, B <= 4 T, degree {deg}:\\n' + local.summary())
            for tone in local.tones:
                if 6 < tone.freq < 8:
                    ax[0].plot(tone.b_centers, tone.snr, 'o-', label=f'{tone.freq:.2f} T, degree {deg}')
        cuts = (1.03, 1.5, 2.0)
    else:
        cuts = (on.onset_b, 1.0, 1.5)
        for tone in on.tones[:3]:
            ax[0].plot(tone.b_centers, tone.snr, 'o-', label=f'{tone.freq:.2f} T')
    ax[0].axhline(5, color='k', ls=':'); ax[0].set(xlabel='B (T)', ylabel='matched-filter SNR', yscale='log'); ax[0].legend(fontsize=8)
    for cutoff in cuts:
        for deg in (3,5):
            f, spec = sdh_fft(R[:,None], B, b_range=(cutoff,10), bg_degree=deg, nfft=2048, log=False)
            band = (f > 3) & (f < 65)
            norm = spec[0,band].max()
            ax[1].plot(f, spec[0]/norm, label=f'B>={cutoff:.2f}, degree {deg}')
            pk, _ = find_peaks(spec[0]); pk = [p for p in pk if band[p]]
            pk = sorted(pk, key=lambda p:-spec[0,p])[:5]
            print(f'FFT cutoff={cutoff:.2f} degree={deg}: candidate peaks {[round(float(f[p]),2) for p in pk]} T')
    ax[1].axvline(abs(n)*10.33916924, color='k', ls=':', label='nominal g=4 F_L')
    ax[1].set(xlim=(0,65), ylim=(0,1.15), xlabel='F (T)', ylabel='FFT / max above 3 T')
    ax[1].legend(fontsize=7); fig.suptitle(f'Run {rid}: onset and FFT sensitivity, signed R; no B symmetrization available')
    fig.tight_layout(); plt.show()
PY
