# Four legs, each gate 0 -> each card limit with the other parked at 0, 101 pts, delay 1 s,
# nplci=10 on the gate-current channels (pA floor). Lock-in X on sr1 (B_1-B_2) + sr0 (drain)
# answer "is the device alive on the provided contacts"; gate currents answer "is it safe".
# Automatic abort: |I_gate| > 1 nA on either Keithley trips the sweep (no operator eyes in E1).
from sharpelab_nb.autorange import autorange_sr830s

# --- preconditions (state this cell assumes but does not set) ---
assert_thermometry_live("T_sample", VTI.temp_logfile_candidates["T_sample"], max_age=15, max_period=12)
_T0 = T_sample(); _B0 = magnet.field()
print(f"precondition T_sample = {_T0:.3f} K (expect 1.0-1.5), B = {_B0:+.4f} T (expect |B|<0.02), "
      f"V_tg = {k_tg.volt():+.3f}, V_bg = {k_bg.volt():+.3f}, V_si = {k_si():+.3f} V (expect 0)")
assert 1.0 <= _T0 <= 1.5, f"T_sample {_T0} K off base"
assert abs(_B0) < 0.02, f"magnet not at zero: {_B0} T"
assert abs(k_si()) < 0.01, "Si gate not at 0"

legs = [(k_tg, TG_MAX), (k_tg, TG_MIN), (k_bg, BG_MAX), (k_bg, BG_MIN)]
n_pts, delay = 101, 1.0
I_TRIP = 1e-9   # A — hard abort threshold on either gate current

# pA-floor readback on the gate-current channels (reset at the end if no leg tripped)
k_tg.nplci(10); k_bg.nplci(10)

# sr1 sensitivity sized for an unknown Rxx: 500 uV = 50 kOhm full scale at I_bias = 10 nA
# (drive 1 V / 100 MOhm, as the operator set it); autorange hook tracks from there.
sr1.sensitivity(500e-6)
print(f"drive {sr1.amplitude()} V @ {sr1.frequency()} Hz -> I_bias ~ {sr1.amplitude()/100e6*1e9:.1f} nA; "
      f"sr0 sens {sr0.sensitivity()} V, sr1 sens {sr1.sensitivity()} V, tau {sr1.time_constant()} s")

tripped = []
for gate, v_end in legs:
    other = k_bg if gate is k_tg else k_tg
    mc = dict(meas_config); mc["comments"] = f"gate-current-sanity-check: {gate.name} 0 -> {v_end:+g} V, other gate 0, Si 0, B 0"
    s = sweep.AsyncStation(mc)
    s.add_comment('gate-current-sanity-check')
    s.add_comment(f'gate: {gate.name}; leg: 0 -> {v_end:+g} V (card limit); {other.name} parked 0; Vsi = 0; B = 0')
    s.ramp(k_tg.volt, 0); s.ramp(k_bg.volt, 0)
    xp = gate.volt
    # row layout: [time, setpoint, other.volt, gate.curr, other.curr, T_sample, sr0.X, sr0.P, sr1.X, sr1.P]
    s.fp(other.volt).fp(gate.curr).fp(other.curr).fp(T_sample)
    s.fp(sr0.X).fp(sr0.P).fp(sr1.X).fp(sr1.P)
    s.plot(xp, k_tg.curr); s.plot(xp, k_bg.curr)
    s.plot(xp, sr1.X); s.plot(xp, sr0.X)
    s.register_run_before(autorange_sr830s, (sr0, [sr1]))

    def leak_guard(station, data, _gate=gate):
        i_g, i_o = abs(float(data[3])), abs(float(data[4]))
        if i_g > I_TRIP or i_o > I_TRIP:
            print(f"LEAK TRIP on {_gate.name} leg at V = {float(data[1]):+.3f} V: |I_swept| = {i_g:.3e}, |I_other| = {i_o:.3e} A")
            tripped.append((_gate.name, float(data[1]), i_g, i_o))
            station.interrupt_requested = True
    s.register_run_after(leak_guard, ())

    try:
        s.sweep(gate.volt, np.linspace(0, v_end, n_pts), delay=delay)
    finally:
        s.ramp(gate.volt, 0)
    if tripped:
        break

if tripped:
    print("STOP — a leg tripped the leakage guard; nplci left at 10, gates parked at 0:", tripped)
else:
    k_tg.nplci(1); k_bg.nplci(1)
    print("all four legs ran without a leakage trip; nplci reset to 1")
    print("k_tg.volt validator:", k_tg.volt.vals, "| k_bg.volt validator:", k_bg.volt.vals)

def multimegasweep(
        self,
        slow_params: list[Parameter],
        slow_v_list: list[Setpoints],
        fast_params: list[Parameter],
        fast_v_list: list[Setpoints],
        slow_delay: float = 0.0,
        fast_delay: float = 0.0,
        init_delay: bool = True,
    ) -> SweepResult:
        self._check_interrupted()
        if not all(len(sp) == len(fast_v_list[0]) for sp in fast_v_list):
            raise ValueError("not all fast axis setpoint lists have same length!")
        if not all(len(sp) == len(slow_v_list[0]) for sp in slow_v_list):
            raise ValueError("not all slow axis setpoint lists have same length!")

        slow_vs = [list(i) for i in zip(*slow_v_list)]
        fast_vs = [list(i) for i in zip(*fast_v_list)]

        with (
            self._sweep_context(),
            sweep.db.Writer(self._basedir) as w,
            self._plotter as p,
        ):
            self.logger.info(f"Starting multimegasweep with ID {w.id}")
            slowparamlist: list[str] = []
            for param in slow_params:
                slowparamlist.append(param.full_name)

            fastparamlist: list[str] = []
            for param in fast_params:
                fastparamlist.append(param.full_name)

            self.logger.debug(f"Slows: {slowparamlist}, Fasts: {fastparamlist}")
            min_duration = (
                len(slow_vs) * len(fast_vs) * fast_delay + len(slow_vs) * slow_delay
            )
            self.logger.info(f"Minimum duration {_sec_to_str(min_duration)}")

            self._init_metadata(
                w,
                type="2D",
                function="multimegasweep",
                slow_delay=slow_delay,
                fast_delay=fast_delay,
                slow_params=slowparamlist,
                fast_params=fastparamlist,
                columns=["time"] + slowparamlist + fastparamlist + self._col_names(),
                slow_setpoints=[list(sps) for sps in slow_v_list],
                fast_setpoints=[list(sps) for sps in fast_v_list],
            )
            p.set_cols(w.metadata["columns"])

            for i, slow_v in enumerate(_progress(slow_vs, position=0)):
                self.logger.debug(f"{i + 1}/{len(slow_vs)}: {slowparamlist} = {slow_v}")
                for slow_param, ov in zip(slow_params, slow_v):
                    slow_param(ov)

                for j, fast_v in enumerate(_progress(fast_vs, position=1, leave=False)):
                    for fast_param, iv in zip(fast_params, fast_v):
                        fast_param(iv)

                    if not init_delay and i == 0 and j == 0:
                        pass
                    elif j == 0:
                        interruptible_sleep(
                            slow_delay,
                            show_progress=False,
                            should_stop=self._should_stop,
                        )

                    if self._should_stop():
                        self.logger.warning(f"ID {w.id} INTERRUPTED")
                        self._interrupted = True
                        w.metadata["interrupted"] = True
                        break

                    time.sleep(fast_delay)

                    self._run_run_befores(
                        station=self,
                        writer=w,
                    )

                    data = [time.time()] + slow_v + fast_v + self._measure()
                    w.add_point(data)
                    p.add_point(data)

                    self._run_run_afters(
                        station=self,
                        data=data,
                        writer=w,
                    )

                    if self._should_stop():
                        self.logger.warning(f"ID {w.id} INTERRUPTED")
                        self._interrupted = True
                        w.metadata["interrupted"] = True
                        break

                if self._should_stop():
                    self.logger.warning(f"ID {w.id} INTERRUPTED")
                    self._interrupted = True
                    w.metadata["interrupted"] = True
                    break

            w.metadata["end_time"] = time.time()
            image = p.send_image()
            if image is not None:
                w.add_blob("plot.png", image)
                display.display(display.Image(data=image, format="png"))

        duration = w.metadata["end_time"] - w.metadata["start_time"]
        self.logger.info(f"Completed in {_sec_to_str(duration)}")
        self.logger.info(f"Data saved in {w.datapath}")

        return SweepResult(self._basedir, w.id, cast(Metadata, w.metadata), w.datapath)

# Extracting tetralayer-graphene stacking order from magnetotransport — a survey

*A grounded review of how to distinguish the tetralayer (N = 4) graphene
stacking orders — ABAB (Bernal), ABCA (rhombohedral), ABCB (mixed) — by
transport, and the measurement method it motivates. Synthesises four ingested
references — Min–MacDonald 2008 (`papers/0711.4333/paper.md`, chiral
decomposition), Koshino–McCann 2011 (`papers/1104.0794/paper.md`,
full-parameter Bernal-N LLs), Grushina et al. 2015
(`papers/1501.06764/paper.md`, Bernal-4L experiment), Kalantre et al. 2026
(`papers/2606.05356/paper.md`, R4G fermiology + model). Companion to the
trilayer survey (`stacking-extraction-survey.md`), whose method framework —
F_L combinatorics, scale pinning, harmonic screen, per-channel reads — carries
over unchanged; this survey carries only what is N = 4-specific. The
operational decision procedure lives in
`recipes/investigations/tetralayer-stacking-fs-count.md`.*

> **Provenance and strength conventions** (`recipes/STYLE.md`): **paper-data**
> · **citation** · **our-model** · **heuristic**; calls use **decisive ·
> strong · weak · consistent-with · uninformative**.

---

## 1. The three stackings and their decomposition

2^(N−2) = 4 raw sequences collapse to **three distinct tetralayer orders**
(theory-paper, `papers/0711.4333` Table I; ABCB ≡ ABAC read end-to-end):

| Stacking | Chiral blocks | Low-energy bands | CNP at D = 0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| **ABAB** (Bernal) | J = 2 ⊕ 2 | two bilayer-like parabolic pairs, masses ∝ λγ₁ with λ = 1.618 / 0.618 | semimetallic; e–h overlap structure at γ₂ scale; interaction gap in ultraclean devices (§5) |
| **ABCA** (rhombohedral) | J = 4 | single quartic (k⁴ + trigonal warping) flat-bottomed band | gapless; gaps under D |
| **ABCB** (mixed, metastable) | J = 3 ⊕ 1 | cubic (k³) + linear (k) Dirac-like pair | **intrinsic** gap ≈ 9 meV (citation: Wirth et al., arXiv:2203.07971 — not yet ingested) |

Two symmetry facts with consequences (theory-paper, `papers/1104.0794`):
even-N Bernal has **no mirror plane**, so ABAB's two bilayer blocks are mixed
by γ₂/γ₅ even at D = 0 — the two-Fermi-surface picture is exact only above
the ~20 meV remote-hopping scale, and inter-block magnetic breakdown is
symmetry-allowed (unlike trilayer's parity-protected ML/BL). Even-N *does*
have inversion symmetry, forcing **valley degeneracy** of the ABAB spectrum
at D = 0 (trilayer's low LLs valley-split; ABAB's do not until D breaks
inversion).

## 2. Primary discriminator — the FS count against F_L

Same read as the trilayer method: enumerate resolved SdH tones, screen
harmonics, and match the peak *set* against the Luttinger frequency
F_L = (h/4e)·n (g = 4 while degeneracies are unbroken). The N = 4 templates:

- **ABCA → a singleton at F_L.** One post-cascade pocket carries the full
  density. Trigonal-warping Lifshitz structure is confined to low density
  (citation: the cascade scale shrinks with N vs the trilayer ~10¹¹ cm⁻²;
  quantitative D = 0 boundaries pending our-model). At the ~10¹² operating
  density: one surface.
- **ABAB → a pair partitioning F_L at ≈ 0.72 / 0.28.** Parabolic bands at a
  shared E_F populate ∝ mass, and the block masses scale with the effective
  couplings λ₃γ₁ / λ₁γ₁ → density (and frequency) ratio λ₃/λ₁ = φ² ≈ 2.62
  (theory-paper, `papers/1104.0794`). That is the parabolic
  (decomposition-limit) value; the full model distorts it both ways —
  γ₂-scale band-bottom offsets at low |n|, non-parabolicity at high |n| —
  and the design numbers are its F(n) table (our-model,
  `models/tetralayer_fs_count`). Two exception regimes: at **low electron
  density** the light pocket nearly empties (0.6 T at +1×10¹²) and the heavy
  tone rides at ≈ 0.95·F_L — the one regime where ABAB genuinely mimics an
  ABCA singleton within the scale prior; on the **near-CNP hole side** the
  semimetal overlap leaves the pair close and balanced ([4.4, 5.9] T at
  −1×10¹²) — a beat, not two resolved tones, on a short 1/B record. Both
  wash out by |n| ≳ 2–3×10¹².
- **ABCB → a pair with a Dirac partner.** Cubic main tone + linear-band
  small tone over the intrinsic gap (theory-paper `papers/0711.4333`;
  magnitude/partition citation-grade until modeled). The J = 1 velocity is
  renormalized below the monolayer value — do not fit the small tone with a
  pristine-Dirac slope.

**Why this is an easier read than the trilayer case**: the trilayer
discriminator hinges on a small (few-%–17%) ML tone because ABA's dominant
tone nearly coincides with ABC's singleton. At N = 4 and design densities
|n| ≳ 2–3×10¹² the dominant tones themselves separate — ABAB's biggest tone
sits at ≈ 0.72–0.79·F_L, well off the ABCA singleton at F_L — and the ABAB
partner tone carries ~21–28% of F_L. Presence *and* position of the dominant
tone discriminate, with the partner tone and Luttinger partition as
confirmation. The low-|n| exception regimes above are where the advantage
evaporates — design around them.

Carried over unchanged from the trilayer method (see that survey and recipe):
pin the global scale on the whole peak set first; classify on frequencies,
never amplitudes; screen harmonics by integer multiples + n-dependence; read
each Rxx channel separately (mosaic flakes); and the **F_L sum-tone
confound** — an ABAB pair's breakdown/mixing tone lands at f₁+f₂ = F_L and

## HERA — first D≈0 electron Landau fan for the stacking investigation

"'`landau-fan-vti` (base `landau-fan`), in-arc under `tetralayer-stacking-fs-count` steps 2–5. Gates A/B remain green in the same kernel: setup/SAFETIES measure cells 2–27, VERIFY 32, operator handoff readback 44 and binding probe 46; Gate C passed in runs 0–3 (ana 10–11). Runs 6–7 are now analyzed raw-first in ana 14–15. Choose the electron side because the available high density separates the model templates and reproduces run 6 at n_A=3.2; the hole range stops near −1.27 and its close low-density pair is harder to interpret. The committed calibration is the run-5 ratio c_bg/c_tg≈0.773, geometry-prior absolute scale, n_offset=−0.0894×10¹², D_offset=−0.013 V/nm; use the identical rounded coefficients used for run 6 so the shared-density gate settings match.

**Claim and uncertainty.** This is a narrow density-dependence and sampling-reproduction measurement on the hardwired B_1−B_2 channel, not a preassigned ABAB/ABCA verdict. Run 6 has candidate ≈7, 22, 29–30 T components and higher harmonics; require a global-scale fit to the whole set, Luttinger-aware harmonic screening, ABAB and trilayer dual overlays, and the sum-tone origin audit before a call. The second CNP ridge does not establish a second stacking domain. Only positive B is measured; odd-in-B contamination and unresolved spatial contributions remain hedges.

**Onset is an extraction fork.** The full 0.3–10 T polynomial analysis returns a censored 0.30 T edge, while the large high-field MR contaminates the low-frequency background. On the existing low-field-only 0.3–4 T record, `sdh_onset(..., b_hi=4, bg_degree=5, r_full_scale=5000)` gives **1.0309097 T**, carried by the ≈6.7 T component; degree 3 gives that component 1.04 T but marks it marginal, with the 22 T headline at 1.38 T. This fan uses the measured local onset provisionally, not the censored full-record edge as a physical onset. It cannot establish whether useful oscillations exist below 1.03 T. Reproduction at n=3.2 and a post-fan per-column onset audit are required; if the useful window starts higher, recompute resolution and downgrade the call, never count sub-onset rows as signal. A lower-field extension remains the deciding measurement for this onset fork.

**Binding design math (nominal run-5 density scale).** Direct `fs_count_b0.abab_fs(n*1e16)` gives the ABAB pair **6.038/22.914 T at n=2.8**, and **7.306/25.783 T at n=3.2**; ABCA F_L is **28.950→33.085 T**. The inverse-field record is **0.828173 T⁻¹**, δF=**1.2075 T**: the lowest-density partner gets **5.0004 periods**, and the ≥6.038 T heavy-ABAB/ABCA split exceeds 2δF=2.415 T. Solving the five-period condition at n=2.8 gives B_max≥7.0465 T; use 7.05 T, without paying the additional 21.5 min bare traverse to 10 T. This five-period statement is nominal, not guaranteed over the density-scale prior or a later-onset column; fit the scale globally and re-evaluate it in the read.

**Both-axis Nyquist and cost floor.** Uniform 1/B: **217 rows**, Δ(1/B)=**0.0038341 T⁻¹**, Nyquist **130.41 T**. This clears the nominal F_L≤33.09 T, its +20% scale allowance and the measured higher-frequency candidates up to ≈130 T from run 6; those candidates need not be pockets, but allowing them to alias into the low-tone band would invalidate the read. Density: **11 points**, Δn=**0.04×10¹² cm⁻²**; even with +20% scale, 0.048 is below the lowest-field ray-Nyquist bound B_lo/(2×10.339)=**0.04985×10¹²**. Total **2,387 points**. Gate vectors round-trip to D=0: TG **0.8690→0.9836 V**, BG **1.0178→1.1661 V**, Si stays 0 V. No clamping and no validator, gate pacing, field-cap or temperature-cap changes.

**Settling and dynamic range.** Preserve 10 nA, τ=0.3 s and 24 dB/oct; **fast_delay=3 s=10τ**, slow_delay=1 s plus the driver'"'s 3 s field settle. Set sr1 to the spot-check's **50 µV (5 kΩ nominal full scale)**, not the 2 µV restored at handoff; sr0 remains 20 mV. Run 6 peaks at 530 Ω over the larger 0–10 T range; scaling by 3.2/2.8 and a further factor 3 gives a conservative heuristic 1.82 kΩ corner budget, below full scale. This is a headroom estimate, not measured low-density MR; abort at 90% range. Record and plot both temperatures, both gate currents, both wired lock-ins' X and phase, and actual field; n.c. sr2/sr3 are not measured.

**Price and coverage trade.** Run 5 measured 1.098 s median / 1.116 s p90 per point with 1 s dwell and NPLC=1. Budget **3.2 s/point** here for 3 s dwell, paired-gate writes and added readbacks: **127.3 min** acquisition. Total 0→7.05 T travel is **7.05×7.3=51.5 min**, including **7.53 min positioning** to the first row; runs 6/7 measured ≈3.08 s overhead per field point, so budget that per row plus 1 s slow delay and ≈0.5 s paired-gate flyback (**16.6 min**). Subtotal ≈195 min; allow ≈15% for overhead variation and preflight → headline rounded to 3 h 50 min. The full accessible D=0 gate line (−1.27→+3.27) at the same conservative sampling would require about 111 density points and >22 h, while its low-density partner would still fail the period requirement. We exclude that region and the hole side explicitly. Even n=2.7 needs B≈10.41 T for five nominal partner periods at this onset, outside the committed 10 T cap. The selected 0.4×10¹² span limits branch-trajectory discrimination; a calibrated cannot-tell remains an acceptable outcome.

**Checkpoints and endpoint.** Inspect the first three landed rows (roughly 10–12 min including positioning) for leakage, clipping, dead channels, current and field tracking. Then inspect every ~25 rows / 20 min; automatic per-point guards stop on >1 nA gate current, clipping, loss of current, off-base temperature, nonfinite data or >20 mT field mismatch; each row checks thermometry freshness (15 s age, 12 s cadence). At B≈3 T (about row 167), compare the n=3.2 column with run 6 over the same field window and attempt the first resolution-qualified FFT; abandon if adequate data cannot reproduce its oscillations or if acquisition quality fails. Keep the live "'`hera-watch` digest armed throughout. On normal completion, hold **7.05 T and the n=3.2 gates** for analysis and a possible downward follow-up; no unrequested retraverse or state0 replay. On a stop, re-read actual state and notify Zack; VTI kernel interrupt does **not** stop a supply ramp, so an in-progress magnet ramp requires operator intervention at the instrument. Close-out remains the brief'"'s separate return-to-initial question.
